one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience.

My family has dealt with this property for many years, and my mother operated her hair salon from the premises for 46 years. After recently closing the salon, I became aware of serious concerns regarding the way the property had apparently been managed.

My mother advised me that the landlord or his representatives had not entered the premises for approximately 20 years, with no regular inspections or compliance testing during that time. When issues were reported, they were not properly addressed.

As a landlord myself, I understand that owning a commercial property comes with responsibilities and obligations. I find it extremely concerning that a tenant can occupy a property for decades while apparently receiving so little attention from the property owner.

There is also an outstanding invoice relating to structural repairs that I arranged and paid for. I was advised that I would be reimbursed for these costs, yet the invoice remains unpaid.

What is also concerning is my experience of the business’s online reviews. I have noticed that negative reviews that were previously visible appear to have been removed, while the website now appears to display predominantly, if not exclusively, 5-star reviews. This gives a very different impression from the experience we have had.

I have tried to resolve the matter directly and reasonably, but I am now seeking further advice regarding the outstanding invoice and the concerns surrounding the property.

This is no longer simply about the money. It is about principle, honesty and honouring an agreement.

After 46 years of my mother being a tenant, I expected much better communication, accountability and professionalism.

A very disappointing experience, and certainly not the way I believe a landlord or property manager should treat a long-standing tenant.

I asked for curtain bangs and a layered haircut and showed the stylist pictures and videos of exactly what I wanted. I can barely see any layers at the back, and my hair looks almost the same as it did when I entered the salon. The entire haircut took approximately five minutes, yet I was charged the full amount.

Unfortunately, my boyfriend’s experience was just as upsetting. His stylist was rude and did not listen to what he asked for, even though he also showed reference pictures and videos. His hair was cut far shorter than requested, and he now feels he has to wear a cap because he is so unhappy with it.

We clearly explained what we wanted and asked beforehand whether the stylists were able to do these haircuts. They said yes, but the results showed a serious lack of care, attention and skill. This was a deeply disappointing experience, and I would not recommend this salon based on the service and results we received.

Very disappointing experience with Specsavers Craigieburn.

I first went to Specsavers in May to get my glasses. Unfortunately, the colour of the frames was incorrect when they arrived after approximately three weeks. I was told they could change them, which they eventually did.

However, once I started wearing the glasses, my eyes constantly felt tired and the glasses simply didn’t feel right. I returned in June to explain the problem. The customer service staff member briefly looked at the glasses and told me they were fine. Adam then looked at them and adjusted them, but I was told that my eyes were simply getting used to the glasses and that I should give them some time.

I continued using them for around two weeks, but I started experiencing migraines, so I stopped wearing them.

I then made another appointment, this time for today at 12:20pm. They contacted me and asked me to come in around 12pm so they could look into the issue. The optometrist I saw was actually very good. She listened to me, explained everything clearly and suggested that I change the glasses because they may simply feel too heavy for me.

She asked me to sit down and wait while this was looked into. I sat there waiting until around 1:30pm. During this time, several customer service staff members were around, and although they could see me waiting, nobody came over to explain what was happening or provide any update.

Eventually, another optometrist came over and told me they could not change the glasses because there was supposedly nothing wrong with them. What I found particularly upsetting was the way my concerns were handled. I felt as though I was being accused of making up or lying about the migraines and discomfort I had been experiencing.

I have now attended multiple appointments regarding the same pair of glasses, and after all this time, I am still left with glasses that I cannot comfortably wear.

I expect much better customer service and communication, especially when a customer has made several appointments and is genuinely experiencing discomfort. Even if Specsavers believed there was nothing technically wrong with the glasses, I expected my concerns to be listened to respectfully and for someone to properly explain the options available to me.

Very disappointing experience overall, particularly with the customer service at Specsavers Craigieburn.

one_star_reviews.text:
WHAT A BUNCH OF LOSERS LOOK ELSEWHERE

I spent approximately $70,000 on flooring from Bowens in Hastings, installed by my builder.

Just over a year later, several individual planks have become badly discoloured and appear to be delaminating. Not the entire floor. Not an area that has been flooded. Specific individual planks.

Bowens inspected the problem and concluded that it was caused by water damage.

An interesting diagnosis, given that there has been no water damage.

Apparently water in my house possesses remarkable powers of discrimination: it can pass over perfectly good floorboards, select an individual plank for destruction, leave its neighbours largely untouched, and then quietly disappear without leaving any other evidence of its visit.

Perhaps I have unusually sophisticated water.

Whatever the explanation, what disappoints me most is Bowens' response. When someone spends around $70,000 on a product, I don't think it is unreasonable to expect the supplier to take an apparent product failure seriously, investigate it properly and stand behind what they sell.

Instead, my experience has essentially been: it's water damage, therefore not our problem.

If this is representative of Bowens' approach to customer service when something goes wrong, I would be extremely reluctant to buy anything substantial from them again.

And I certainly couldn't recommend them to anyone contemplating a major purchase.

Selling $70,000 worth of flooring is the easy part. How a company behaves when that flooring starts falling apart is where you discover what you actually bought.

Despite following the clinic’s own advice and cancelling because the required report was not available, we were still charged a cancellation fee.

I later raised the matter with Pieta, the clinic manager, and found the response extremely disappointing. There seemed to be very little understanding or consideration of the circumstances, even though this situation was outside our control and we had communicated with the clinic throughout.

For a long-standing patient, it is upsetting to feel that common sense, fairness and basic compassion were missing in the way this was handled. Policies are important, but there should also be room to consider genuine circumstances, particularly when a patient has acted on the advice of clinic staff.

At the end of the day, this is not about the money. It is about the principle of the matter, fairness, and having some basic human understanding when circumstances are clearly outside a patient’s control.

Unfortunately, this experience has significantly changed my view of the clinic. I would encourage anyone considering this clinic to make sure they are very clear about the cancellation policy, even when circumstances are outside their control.

one_star_reviews.text:
Poor Workmanship & Unacceptable Service Quality

I purchased a brand-new Toyota HiAce on 17 August 2026. On the day of delivery, I noticed a crack in the middle of the front windshield. I immediately contacted Toyota, and a week later, I brought the vehicle to Waverley Toyota - Spare Parts and Service Centre for its 1,000 km check and windshield replacement. A service advisor named Gihan attended to me.

Here is what happened during this process:

1. Poor Workmanship & Cleaning After Service:
I picked up the vehicle late afternoon after the first windshield replacement. Upon returning home, I found black sealant debris and fine glass fragments scattered across the dashboard. It took me 20 minutes with a vacuum cleaner just to clean it up.

2. Water Leakage:
That very night, after light rain in Melbourne, the newly fitted windshield leaked. Water leaked through the interior roof light, dripped directly onto the Multi-Purpose Front Camera assembly, and overflowed down onto the gear shift assembly.

3. Poor Communication & Broken Promises:
I brought the car back to Gihan immediately. A second windshield replacement was required. Gihan initially promised a courtesy vehicle, but an hour later, he called back to say no loan car could be provided and told me to contact my original sales representative instead. Bouncing customers around and breaking commitments shows a total lack of professionalism.

4. Worse Condition & Poor Seal Fitting on Second Attempt (See Photos):
I waited a week, explicitly reminding Gihan to ensure proper cabin protection this time. He assured me it would be handled properly. On Thursday, 3 September, I collected the vehicle. Unbelievably, the dashboard was again covered in countless black sealant debris—even worse and more scattered than after the first replacement. Furthermore, the external rubber moulding and sealant fitting is warped, uneven, and poorly installed along the roof edge (see attached photos). When I raised immediate objections on-site, Gihan considered this an acceptable and normal situation. He then told me that if I had any further issues, I should contact my original sales representative directly.

Conclusion:
Toyota prides itself on quality, but delivering a vehicle with a leaking windshield, poor seal fitting, and failing twice in a row to protect the cabin is unacceptable.

I have documented all photos, timelines, and communications. I require an official response from Toyota Management detailing how this matter will be properly resolved.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a roller door installed by Nuevo Garage Doors approximately 18 months ago, and unfortunately my experience has been extremely disappointing.

From the beginning, communication was difficult. I was told I would receive a call over the weekend to confirm the installation date because there were things I needed to prepare beforehand. That call never came, and the installer subsequently arrived without confirmation and became angry that the preparation had not been completed.

The door itself arrived with scratches, which I raised at the time. When it was spray-painted, paint was also sprayed onto my exterior brickwork.

The biggest issue, however, has developed since installation.

I am not in the building industry and know very little about ceilings. I have since been told that the garage ceiling was already sagging when the roller door was installed and that ceilings in this situation can continue to sag. The problem is now so significant that the roller door can barely be opened because it hits the ceiling. It has also caused scratches to the door from repeatedly hitting the ceiling.

My concern is this: if the installer knew the ceiling was already sagging and knew it was likely to continue sagging, why was the roller door installed without advising me that the ceiling needed to be repaired first?

Had I been properly advised at the time, I could have addressed the ceiling before installing the door. Instead, I now have a roller door that I cannot properly use and a ceiling that needs to be repaired, with the additional cost and complication of having the roller door removed first.

I have now been quoted $550 by Nuevo Garage Doors simply to remove and reinstall the door so the ceiling can be addressed. I have also been told it will not necessarily be reinstalled in exactly the same way due to it's age, which is concerning. Additionally after hearing about all his problems and busyness, I was then told they were too busy, that they couldn't do it for months, and essentially that I should find someone else, the company he used to work for who has quoted me $950 to remove and then replace the roller door so the ceiling can be repaired.

That leaves me in an incredibly difficult position. I have paid for a garage door that is now unusable, and I am being left to organise and pay for the work required to make it possible to use it again.

Unfortunately, the communication throughout this process has also been very difficult. I have experienced being talked over, interrupted and spoken to in an unnecessarily aggressive and dismissive manner. There has been a consistent sense that problems are someone else's responsibility rather than something they are willing to take accountability for.

At one point, I actually had my teenage son come outside and stay with me during a conversation because I found the interaction so difficult and felt I needed someone else present.

I would strongly recommend getting independent advice about the condition of your garage before proceeding with a roller door installation, and making sure any concerns about the existing structure are clearly addressed in writing beforehand.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Lumex has been extremely disappointing.

The most concerning part is not simply that the installation remains incomplete. It is how Lumex has handled the situation after I sought clarification directly from them.

I spoke directly with a Lumex representative about the installation requirements and expectations. During that conversation, I was given a clear position about what was required. I understood that to be Lumex's position.

I then communicated that position to the authorised reseller.

Lumex subsequently gave the reseller a materially different account of what had been discussed and disputed the position that had been communicated to me directly.

This is where the situation became particularly concerning.

By changing or disputing the position communicated to me, Lumex has effectively put me in the position of having to defend what I was told by its own representative. It has created the impression that I have misunderstood, misrepresented or invented what was said.

I relied on what Lumex's representative told me and communicated that information to the authorised reseller in good faith.

The issue is not academic. The position taken affects who is responsible for completing the work and potentially who bears the cost of doing so.

My experience therefore leaves me questioning whether Lumex's response has been influenced by the commercial interests of its authorised reseller. Whatever the reason, Lumex gave me one position directly and subsequently gave its reseller a materially different account.

That leaves a simple question. When the manufacturer's position changes after the customer communicates what the manufacturer told them, who is the customer supposed to rely on?

If Lumex appoints and authorises resellers to sell and install its products, customers should be able to expect Lumex to stand behind its own representations and the products sold under its brand.

Instead, I have had to chase the manufacturer for answers, establish its position myself, and then defend my own account of a conversation with Lumex against a conflicting account subsequently provided to its reseller.

At the time of writing, the system remains incomplete. It has not been properly demonstrated. The handover has not been completed.

Customers should not have to put themselves in the middle of a dispute between a manufacturer and its authorised reseller. They certainly should not be left feeling as though they are the problem for relying on what the manufacturer's own representative told them.

My experience has left me questioning whether Lumex has prioritised maintaining its relationship with its authorised reseller over providing the customer with a consistent and accountable position.

Whatever the reason, the result is the same. Lumex's change in position has escalated the dispute and left me having to defend the accuracy of what I was told by Lumex in the first place.

That is a serious concern for anyone considering purchasing a Lumex system.

Based on my experience, I would approach Lumex with considerable caution.

Extremely disappointing experience at Australia Post Clyde.

I specifically went there to have a passport photo taken for my newborn, only to be told after arriving that they would not take photos of newborn babies. This was incredibly frustrating, especially when travelling with a newborn is not exactly easy.

What makes the experience worse is the lack of clear information. Australia Post’s own website states that participating Post Offices can take passport photos of children and infants and even provides guidance for parents bringing babies in for photos. If this particular branch has decided that it will not provide this service for newborns, that restriction should be clearly stated online or in the branch information so parents can know BEFORE making the trip.

I completely understand if staff at a particular location do not have the equipment or ability to safely take a newborn’s photo. What I don’t understand is advertising passport photo services without clearly communicating such an important limitation.

Parents of newborns already have enough to organise without making unnecessary trips because essential information hasn’t been provided.

Very poor communication and a genuinely frustrating experience. Please update your service information so other parents don’t waste their time.

one_star_reviews.text:
Think twice before buying Longchamp. Premium prices, disappointing quality, and even worse customer service.

I’ve been buying Longchamp for years and have owned several of their bags. Some have lasted over a decade, so I never expected a backpack to start falling apart in less than six months.

The stitching around the zipper of my Le Pliage One M Backpack came apart during normal use. It wasn’t overloaded or misused. For a bag that costs around AUD $300, this is simply unacceptable.

I took it to the Longchamp Chadstone boutique expecting them to inspect the fault properly. Instead, I was told I’d have to pay AUD $90 for a repair because it was outside their 3-month repair policy. That was the only answer I was given.

The most disappointing part was the customer service. My concerns were brushed aside and there was no genuine interest in investigating whether the product itself was faulty.

I then contacted Longchamp Australia. The replies from customer service representative Kayla felt like generic template emails that ignored most of the points I had raised. Despite providing photos and explaining that the bag failed within six months under normal use, I received the same policy-based response instead of a meaningful assessment.

Under Australian Consumer Law, consumers are entitled to products that are of acceptable quality and reasonably durable. A company’s internal policy does not override those rights. Longchamp seemed far more interested in repeating its policy than addressing a legitimate quality issue.

This isn’t about AUD $90. It’s about accountability. When a premium brand sells a premium-priced product, it should stand behind its quality and treat customers with respect when something goes wrong.

After this experience with both the Chadstone store and Longchamp Australia’s customer service, I’ve lost confidence in Longchamp as a brand, not just this store.

I won’t be buying Longchamp again, and I wouldn’t recommend anyone spend their money on this brand, whether in Australia or anywhere else. There are plenty of brands that offer better quality and much better after-sales service.

Save your money and buy from a brand that actually stands behind its products.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Kärcher Australia.

I dropped my premium commercial pressure washer in for repair on 11 June. More than two months later, I’m still waiting to get it back.

The communication has been appalling. I have had to chase Kärcher at virtually every stage, emails have repeatedly gone unanswered, and even promised callbacks simply never happened. I approved the repair on 20 July and was told parts had been ordered, then heard absolutely nothing for almost a month until I chased them again.

I also have very little confidence in their diagnosis. This is an expensive commercial machine that has had extremely light, almost exclusively residential use at my own home, yet has suffered multiple failures. Kärcher blamed things including my hose setup and a modified plug, but despite repeatedly questioning how these actually caused the failures, I was never given an explanation that I found convincing.

The final straw was calling to escalate the complaint and being told there was nobody I could speak to and no phone number they could give me — only another email address. This is particularly frustrating when unanswered emails are one of the reasons I’m complaining in the first place.

I eventually had to go to Bunnings and buy another pressure washer because I simply couldn’t wait any longer.

For such a large and well-known brand, I’m genuinely astounded by how poorly this has been handled.

I spent the extra money on Kärcher because I thought I was buying premium equipment backed by a premium company. This experience has completely changed my opinion of the brand. They’ve lost me as a customer and I certainly couldn’t recommend them based on the service I’ve received.

one_star_reviews.text:
I recently attended a mediation here, and unfortunately, the experience left me extremely disappointed.

Before attending, I genuinely believed that mediation was supposed to be a fair and impartial process where both parties were given a reasonable opportunity to speak and be heard. Unfortunately, that was not how I experienced it.

I was given roughly 20% of the opportunity to speak and was not even able to fully explain the issues I wanted to raise. The officer then spent significantly most of time with the other party.

What concerned me most was the way the mediation ended. Without giving me any prior notice or an opportunity to respond, the officer came back and told me that the other party had already left. I was then told that the officer was not there to provide a service to me and that she would therefore leave as well.

I fully understand that different parties may need different levels of support during mediation. However, this should not come at the expense of basic fairness, professionalism and the opportunity for both parties to be heard.

I also found it disappointing that, as a male participant, I did not feel that I was treated with the same level of consideration and respect. Being calm, respectful and a gentleman should not mean that you receive less opportunity to speak or less respect in the process.

I do not know whether the officer and the other party knew each other beforehand, and I am not making any allegation about that. However, regardless of any personal circumstances, I believe mediation officers should always maintain professional boundaries and ensure that both parties are treated fairly and impartially.

I am posting this review on behalf of someone who is genuinely concerned about raising these issues directly because he is worried about possible retaliation. Nevertheless, experiences like this should not simply be ignored.

Every person, regardless of gender, deserves to be treated with dignity, respect and fairness during a mediation process. I sincerely hope this feedback is taken seriously and that the organisation reviews how mediation officers ensure both parties are given a fair opportunity to be heard.
Very unsafe organisation to use if you're in a domestic violence situation. Very unsafe. Would give 0 stars if I could.

⚠️ BEWARE – DO NOT USE – SHOULD BE SHUT DOWN!!

Wouldn’t recommend this chemist to a toad!

They were preparing Webster packs for my terminally ill mother when she noticed that one of her tablets looked different from usual. Thank goodness she checked, because the tablet supplied was 100mg higher than her prescribed dose.

When we raised the medication error with the pharmacy, we felt our concerns were simply brushed off rather than being taken seriously. This is incredibly concerning, particularly when dealing with medications for someone who is seriously unwell.

To make matters worse, she was also overcharged by $90. The pharmacy initially attempted to offer a credit, but after what had happened, we insisted on a full refund as we have absolutely no intention of returning.

Mistakes can happen, but when it comes to medication, the consequences can be extremely serious. Patients should be able to trust that their Webster packs contain the correct medications and dosages.

Convenience is not worth compromising on safety. We’ll be driving further to use another local chemist from now on.

Please check your medications carefully, especially if you use Webster packs.

Very disappointing handling of a simple and easily resolved issue.

- The process to book our dog in for cremation was simple. I received confirmation that our payment had been received and was advised of the date our dog would be picked up from our vet. I did not receive any communication after this email.

I was also advised the cremation had now been marked as ‘urgent’. I asked to be contacted when her cremation started.
- I received a phone call 3 days after this email apologising for the delay and was advised “the cremation process has started as we speak” and I should expect it to be completed “on Tuesday” which was in 3 days time.
- My vet called me today (Thursday) stating they had received my dogs ashes today. As we live in rural NSW I believe this is an acceptable time given our distance from Orange/wherever the cremation actually occurs.

The feedback I would give to Pets at Peace is to have better communication with clients. I don’t believe I would’ve received any communication from the company if I hadn’t sent an email asking for an update. I was also under the impression that the “pet tracker” would provide me with updates so I was constantly checking my email/texts. I don’t believe having almost 3 weeks of silence is appropriate in these circumstances.

Google Review

I came to Kmart today to do some shopping.

I purchased all my items, paid for everything and kept my receipt. At the exit, an employee checked my receipt and told me that the plant I had purchased had not been paid for, without even taking the time to properly check the barcode on the item.

I showed him my receipt and calmly asked whether he seriously thought I had not paid for it when the plant was clearly listed on the receipt for $29. Despite this, he continued to question me. The situation started to become frustrating and tense, and he eventually let me leave.

What really bothers me is not the fact that receipts are checked — I completely understand security checks — but the way this situation was handled. I was made to feel as though I had stolen an item, in front of other customers, when a simple and proper check of the receipt would have immediately shown that everything had been paid for.

I also think it would be important to have more properly trained and experienced staff handling these situations, rather than having very young and inexperienced employees carrying out these checks without the necessary professionalism. Being young is obviously not the issue in itself, but the lack of training and professionalism in this situation was very disappointing.

I found the whole experience extremely embarrassing and unacceptable. Security checks can be carried out respectfully and professionally, without accusing a customer of theft before properly checking the facts.

Very disappointing experience. Unfortunately, I will not be returning to this Kmart.

one_star_reviews.text:
ABSOLUTELY UNACCEPTABLE – DO NOT RENT FROM THIS COMPANY

Our experience with this company was absolutely unacceptable, and I would strongly advise anyone considering renting a car from them to think twice.

From the moment we collected the vehicle, we discovered that it was INFESTED with cockroaches. Not one cockroach, but an ongoing infestation inside the vehicle.

We immediately contacted the company and, following their instructions, returned the car so they could treat it. At no point were we offered a replacement vehicle. We were simply given the same vehicle back "after treatment".

When we collected the car again, the problem had NOT been resolved. Cockroaches continued to appear inside the vehicle virtually every day for the remainder of our rental. We had to inspect the car every time before driving and remove cockroaches from inside the vehicle.

The situation became even more disturbing when, while we were driving, a cockroach crawled up my leg. This caused a huge fright and distraction while we were on the road. Thankfully, we did not have an accident, but it could easily have caused one.

Despite all of this, the company did NOT offer to replace the vehicle.

The company's attitude was also extremely disappointing. They treated the presence of cockroaches inside the vehicle as if it were something normal and acceptable. We felt completely dismissed, and at times their attitude towards us was almost as if they found the situation amusing rather than taking our concerns seriously.

They even justified it by saying that German cockroaches are a "common problem in the tropics." Being in a tropical area is not an excuse for providing customers with an infested rental car.

We were later told that we could have returned the car for a refund. But that was not a genuine solution — we had rented the car for 10 days because we needed transportation for our trip. We were never offered a replacement vehicle. We were effectively left with the choice of keeping an infested car or having no rental car at all.

The situation also caused us to miss a pre-booked and paid activity in Kuranda, resulting in additional financial loss and disruption to our holiday.

We paid for a clean, safe and usable rental vehicle. Instead, we received a car infested with cockroaches, a treatment that clearly did not resolve the problem, no replacement vehicle, disruption to our holiday, and an extremely dismissive attitude from the company.

I would absolutely NOT recommend this company. If you are renting a car in Cairns, choose another company.

If you care about your family members, don’t send them to this place. I wouldn’t even trust the staff here to look after my dog.
My mother was sent here for temporary palliative care until a bed became available at Flinders and the treatment she received was more like torture. Due to their negligence, my mother died the next day.

Edit- after speaking to Andrew, who is in charge over all the facilities, I’ve agreed to state that this happened in 2021. What I went through was extremely traumatic and has taken me a long time to actually be able to talk about or process what my mum and I went through, hence my delayed review.
In saying that, I did ask Andrew if when they took over the Vale’s facility, if they replaced all the staff but he pretty much said that’s not practical and couldn’t confirm if the staff are still there from back in 2021. The staff were the issue, irrelevant of who the owner is.
It’s the staff that laid my mum back down straight after vomiting, without helping her clear it out of her throat. It’s the staff who argued about letting me enter the facility at 11pm to check on my mum after her attempting to speak to me on the phone. It’s the staff who, when I asked if they’d called an ambulance cos she was clearly choking, stated they didn’t know what she was supposed to look like. It was the staff, after waiting ages from the ambulance and me asking where it was, that I heard tell the ambulance on the phone that they had checked her vitals and there wasn’t a rush as it wasn’t urgent. It was the staff that couldn’t even answer the ambulance paramedics questions properly or fully which made the paramedics ask me if they could just remove my mum to take her to Flinders as they were disgusted and could see she needed immediate help.
Yes this was all back in 2021 but it’s irrelevant if the owners are new but the staff haven’t been replaced.
I understand that Andrew is concerned about the company’s reputation but what about what my mum went through due to the staff’s negligence? What about the ongoing trauma that I suffer from after seeing my mum suffer like that? I wouldn’t wish that on anyone.
If your family members are there, check in on them and ask them how they are being treated, make sure they are being treated properly and with the dignity that they deserve

I would not recommend this company for emergency leaks.
On a Wednesday afternoon, I arranged for them to attend on Friday, which was their next available appointment. However, they later cancelled because their technician had a family emergency. We then rescheduled for their next available slot on Tuesday, knowing we would be without water over the weekend.
I asked whether they could check if anyone else was available, as we were in a difficult situation. They called on Thursday to advise that a technician was available to attend at 3:00 pm that day. When the technician arrived, he was met by my partner, who advised that work would need to commence by 3:00 pm at the latest.
The technician spent approximately an hour trying to locate the leak but ultimately had to stop when it reached 4:00 pm. He then advised that the job would require two people and that the next available appointment was in 10 days' time.
This was far from ideal, given that we had no water. Although we booked the appointment, we were able to find a plumber who located and fixed the leak by rerunning the entire internal pipework.
We were charged $412 for the one-hour call-out; however, we were no closer to having the issue resolved. In situations like this, I would recommend contacting a plumber first, as they appear to be better equipped to diagnose and resolve the problem.

one_star_reviews.text:
I have always considered Harvey Norman to be a reputable company with excellent customer service, and I would especially like to acknowledge Katrina, who has been extremely helpful, professional and wonderful to deal with.

However, my recent delivery experience was extremely disappointing and frustrating.

The delivery team arrived approximately 45 minutes earlier than the scheduled delivery time and repeatedly called me, pressuring me to be home immediately because it was apparently their last delivery of the day. As a result, I had to cancel an appointment to make sure I was available for the delivery. The delievry folks were rude and arrogant with zero customer service.

Unfortunately, during the delivery of my lounge, the delivery team damaged and broke my front door light. The What made the situation even more frustrating was the conduct of the truck owner afterwards. He repeatedly contacted me by phone asking for details about the damaged light. His manner was aggressive, rude and unprofessional, which made an already disappointing experience even more annoying and stressful.

I eventually had to contact Katrina and ask her to intervene because I did not feel comfortable continuing to deal with the delivery company directly.

To be clear, I have no complaints whatsoever about Katrina or the Harvey Norman staff I have personally dealt with. Katrina has been fantastic and has demonstrated exactly the level of customer service I would expect from a reputable company like Harvey Norman.

My concern is specifically with the delivery company and the way their staff represented Harvey Norman at my home. When a customer purchases furniture from a well-established retailer, the delivery experience is an important part of the overall customer service.

I sincerely hope Harvey Norman reviews the performance of this delivery provider and considers working with professional delivery companies that have proper customer feedback, accountability and review systems in place.

It is very disappointing to have such a positive experience with Harvey Norman staff undermined by an unnecessarily rude, aggressive and unprofessional delivery service.

I hope Harvey Norman takes this feedback seriously and ensures future customers do not have to go through a similarly frustrating and unpleasant experience.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS.  These people are happy to sell you products and provide advice but walk away from any issues that have been encountered when you have followed their advice.  They have alledged that I told them the pavers were wet when the sealer was applied - this is not correct.  I told them the pavers  were wet when they arrived but dryed out (and started to change colour) once they were laid.  The pavers were certainly not wet when the sealer was applied - I am not stupid and would not try and apply any sealer whilst the pavers were wet.  The moisture was contained within the paver - how am I supposed to determine that?  In fact, i asked when I purchased the product and was advised the sealer could be applied immediately, and that I only needed to apply to one side (as it wasn't going around a pool).  There was no mention that the moisture inside the pavers needs to be released prior to coating and there is no mention on the instructions for the sealer.  The supplier stated that "Our team referred you to the product instructions and also offered to contact the supplier if further technical advice was required." - this is an outright lie and no such statement was made.  The initial response from ABC was that they had contacted the manufacturer of the sealer and that the issue was from acid in rain!!  If in fact I had told them I had put the sealer on wet pavers, they would have instantly suggested that was the issue rather than blaming acid rain!  DO NOT TRUST THESE PEOPLE.

EDIT:  ABC have changed their response to my review (why am I not surprised) and now are not claiming I told them the pavers were wet but that they organised for the supplier of the pavers (again suggesting they are in no way responsible) to visit and show me that the issue could be rectified by treating an offcut.  If they had actually tried to contact me they would have known the the offcut used by the supplier of the pavers was not coated with the sealer and therefore was able to be treated appropriately.  What they still fail to address is that they did not tell me (or the instructions on the sealer they sold me say) that I should wait for an extended period to let the moisture in the pavers dry out prior to coating.  I find it amazing that they are responding almost immediately to my negative reviews but have not tried to contact me directly to determine any resolution of the issue.  Whilst it was hidden they did not care but seem to care a lot when it is public.  Tells you everything.

Your comment "We have already spoken with you at length" is complete nonsense.  Please provide me with the details of these "lengthy conversations" and I will happily retract my comments.  You have made it very clear that you have no responsibility in this matter and have made no attempt to contact me to discuss before providing your submissions to Fair Trading. My partner and I have been shopping at this Coles every week for our groceries, but unfortunately, after our repeated experiences with the staff, we will no longer be returning.

The customer service at this store has consistently been disappointing, particularly from some of the older staff members. One staff member in particular, a blonde woman who appears to be in her late 50s to early 60s, has repeatedly spoken to us in a demanding and unpleasant manner.

For example, when purchasing bottled water in bulk, we have been repeatedly instructed that we must scan the water first rather than leaving it until the end. While I understand there may be procedures in place to prevent theft, we are already using the self-checkout and paying for our purchases. Being spoken to as though we are doing something wrong simply because we choose to scan an item at a different point during our shop makes the experience unnecessarily uncomfortable. If the item is scanned and paid for, why should it matter whether it is scanned first or last?

Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. We have experienced poor treatment from staff on a regular basis, to the point where it has become a weekly occurrence.

Just last week, another staff member questioned whether the reusable bags we had with us had been purchased from the store. When my partner confirmed that they had, the staff member insisted that we needed to pay for the bags again. We politely explained that we had already purchased them during our previous shop and, understandably, were not prepared to pay for the same bags twice.

We have been loyal customers and shop here every week, but the repeated negative interactions have completely changed our experience. Customers should not feel uncomfortable or unwelcome when simply trying to do their weekly grocery shopping.

Unfortunately, we will now be taking our weekly shop to Woolworths instead. Very disappointing, Coles.

I wish Google had a negative star rating for companies like this!

This company’s ordering and customer service process is absolutely pathetic.

I placed two orders directly with them, assuming that ordering directly would mean faster delivery. After waiting 2–3 days without receiving any dispatch notification, I had to raise a support ticket myself.

There is no customer service phone number — you can only contact them by email. Eventually, I received a response saying that both orders were on hold and that I needed to provide a photo of the last four digits of my card and a copy of my driver’s licence for verification.

So, apparently, the process is:

1. Customer places an order.
2. Customer waits several days with no shipping notification.
3. Customer has to chase the company through a support ticket.
4. Only then does the company tell you that your order is on hold.
5. Customer is then asked to provide sensitive documents for verification.
6. After submitting everything, you wait again for the accounts team to verify it.
7. Even after verification, there is no guarantee the order will be delivered the next day.

Wow, what a wonderful customer experience!

I provided the requested card information and driver’s licence and waited the entire day. I was then told that the information had been forwarded to the accounts team for verification and that the order may still not be delivered the following day. My only other option was to cancel the order.

I have never experienced such a frustrating ordering process with a company operating in Australia.

This is my first and definitely my last order with this company. Very disappointing experience.

Extremely disappointing experience — ITP Accounting

This is the second, and absolutely last, time I will be using ITP Accounting. After this experience, I cannot see how continuing to use the firm represents the best fiscal use of my fiscal resources.

The biggest disappointment has been the complete lack of communication and professionalism. Sharyn has been particularly hopeless and, from my experience, seems to have simply disappeared when I needed assistance. Trying to get a response has been an exercise in frustration.

Victoria ultimately completed my tax return, but I was extremely disappointed that she chose not to believe me regarding an item I specifically flagged as not being rental income. Even more frustratingly, Victoria appeared to use the ATO as the basis for her position and behaviour, rather than properly considering what I was telling her as the client. I even went to the trouble of forwarding the email from my managing agent which clearly highlighted and supported my position. Despite providing this evidence, I felt as though my explanation was simply disregarded.

As a paying, returning client, I expect my accountant to listen to me, investigate matters properly and work with me to get things right — not make me feel as though I’m having to prove myself or fight to have legitimate information considered.

Unfortunately, my overall impression is that ITP is far more interested in cashing in on clients than genuinely looking after them. The level of communication, customer service and willingness to listen has been incredibly disappointing.

I cannot recommend ITP Accounting to anyone, and I will not be returning as a client. There are plenty of accounting firms that understand that retaining a client requires more than simply charging them a fee — it requires trust, communication, professionalism and actually listening to the person paying the bill.

For me, ITP has failed on all four.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m only writing this review because I hope it can help future patients, particularly anyone who experiences anxiety around medical appointments, and hopefully encourage some consideration around how patients are spoken to.

I had an MRI at Qscan Southport and unfortunately left feeling quite upset, uncomfortable and judged about the way I was spoken to during the screening process.

I was asked whether I had anything that I “wasn’t born with.” I mentioned that I had breast implants, as that was the only thing that came to mind. I was then questioned quite extensively about them. I explained that I couldn’t remember the exact details because I’d had them for a couple of years however I could obtain them if necessary for this procedure. The response was along the lines of, “They would have given you a card,” to which I explained that I hadn’t been given one. I was then told, “Yes, they would have,” followed by, “If I were you, you sound very unsure, so you should get that checked out.”

I found this particularly upsetting and unnecessary. I completely understand the importance of thorough MRI safety screening, and I appreciate that staff need to ask questions to keep patients safe. However, there is a significant difference between appropriately checking a patient’s medical history and making them feel interrogated or as though they have done something wrong.

I also wasn’t thinking to mention things like tattoos or eyelash extensions because, to my understanding, these aren’t automatically contraindications to having an MRI, and I had never been asked about them for previous MRI procedures. What also made me uncomfortable was that the fact I “wasn’t born with” my implants, eyelashes or tattoos which the clinician made a point to reiterate multiple times.

I’m someone who experiences severe anxiety, so I’m very conscious of not wanting to be unfair or unnecessarily critical of healthcare workers. I genuinely appreciate that MRI staff have a responsibility to be cautious and ensure everything is safe. My concern is simply how the questions were communicated and how the interaction made me feel as a patient.

I’m sharing this not to be horrible towards the staff member, but in the hope that Qscan can consider how these conversations are approached, particularly with anxious patients who may already feel nervous about having a medical procedure.

A little more reassurance, patience and kindness would have made a huge difference to my experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Stay clear if you want comfort

I was a tenant with Harcourts Gawler for approximately five years, and unfortunately my experience with their property management was consistently disappointing. After everything that happened during my tenancy and the way my tenancy ended, I would strongly recommend prospective tenants think very carefully before dealing with this office.

When I first moved into the property, the condition was already extremely dirty and run-down. Within the first week, I discovered that touching the shower head could give me an electric shock. It took weeks to resolve, and I remember that the electrical issue ultimately involved investigation/repair around the street power lines. What concerns me most is that there appeared to be no proper documentation of the original issue or repair.

Around 2022, I began experiencing another major problem: the water coming from the taps was brown and visibly dirty. I reported this problem multiple times and was repeatedly told it had supposedly been resolved. It wasn’t. For a significant period of my tenancy, the water remained unusable at times, and I have videos showing brown water coming from multiple taps throughout the property. The underlying problem was only properly addressed towards the end of my tenancy.

The shower screen was another ongoing problem. It broke approximately 3–4 times during my tenancy, with repairs repeatedly being done so cheaply or poorly that the problem would occur again. At one point, the proposed solution was to remove the shower screen and replace it with a shower curtain, despite the bathroom having no proper floor drainage other than the shower.

On another occasion, during repairs, I was effectively left without a usable shower enclosure. I was told I could continue using the shower despite exposed holes and loose/falling tiles. I raised my concerns in writing because I was not comfortable with the safety risks or the potential for water to damage my belongings and the property. Despite this, I was left in that situation for around a week.

Communication throughout the tenancy was also extremely poor. I frequently had to send follow-up emails just to get responses or updates, and there never seemed to be any consistency with who was actually managing the property. It often felt like I had to repeatedly explain the same problems to different people. I still have extensive email correspondence documenting these issues and the way some of them were communicated to me.

Despite putting up with these issues for years, the end of the tenancy was arguably the most frustrating part. I returned the property in better condition than it was when I moved in, yet Harcourts still disputed the condition and attempted to pursue me for various charges, including a $324.50 cleaning charge and $621.64 in alleged rent arrears, which I disputed.

This entire situation occurred while my partner and I were preparing for and then dealing with the arrival of our first child. Instead of being able to move on with our lives, I spent months dealing with a dispute over money and charges that I strongly disputed after an already extremely frustrating five years as a tenant.

I have retained photographs, videos and written correspondence relating to many of the issues described above, including the brown water, maintenance problems and communications with the agency.

What makes the experience even more disappointing is seeing how some negative reviews of this office are responded to publicly. Rather than demonstrating understanding or professionalism, some responses come across as defensive and unnecessarily hostile towards former tenants and home owners.

After approximately five years of renting through Harcourts Gawler, I can honestly say that I would not rent through this office again, and I would not recommend them to anyone looking for a property manager.

For me, this wasn’t one isolated bad experience. It was a pattern of poor maintenance, poor communication and an unnecessarily difficult end to a five-year tenancy.

I was charged $81 by Telstra for a mobile plan that was subsequently cancelled, but I still have not received my refund.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that I provided Telstra with all the information needed to investigate the matter, including the $81 Telstra payment receipt, receipt number, completed cancellation order number, proof of the payment in the My Telstra app, and my account details.

Telstra's own app clearly shows the payment and the completed cancellation, and Telstra support acknowledged that they were not disputing that the $81 charge was made to my credit card. Despite this, their Messaging Team said they could not see the transaction in their system, could not investigate it further, could not raise the matter with the store, and could not arrange the refund.

Instead, I was told that I would need to visit the Telstra Store again.

I already spent a significant amount of my time at the Telstra Store completing paperwork with a Telstra employee. Having provided clear evidence and all relevant transaction details online, I find it extremely disappointing that Telstra cannot internally investigate its own transaction and resolve a straightforward refund through online support.

Customers should not have to repeatedly visit a store or chase different departments because Telstra's internal systems cannot communicate with each other.

Very poor customer experience and an unnecessary waste of time.

I shop at ALDI almost every other day because I appreciate the affordable prices and good value. I don’t expect every staff member to provide perfect customer service, but my recent experiences with a cashier named Rebecca have become unacceptable.

I have repeatedly witnessed her speaking to elderly customers in a very impatient and disrespectful manner. Although she smiles while talking to them, she says things like, “Come on, hurry up,” “People are waiting,” and “People just want to spend their coins in here.” I find this particularly uncomfortable and disrespectful towards elderly customers who may simply need a little more time.

Unfortunately, I have also experienced this behaviour myself. Every time it is my turn at the checkout, she pushes my groceries through the scanner extremely forcefully, including bread and other items that can easily be damaged.

Today was the third time this has happened. She pushed my groceries so hard that my ricotta cheese fell onto the floor. Thankfully, another staff member, an Asian gentleman wearing glasses, kindly came over and helped clean it up. I really appreciate his help.

What disappointed me even more was that Rebecca simply said, “It happens all the time,” rather than acknowledging that her handling of my groceries had caused the problem.

This has happened three times now, and I feel that it is no longer something I should simply ignore. I understand that checkout staff are working under pressure and that the store can be busy, but that does not justify treating customers, especially elderly customers, impatiently or handling their groceries roughly.

I hope ALDI management will take this feedback seriously and look into this staff member’s behaviour. I am not asking for special treatment — I simply expect basic courtesy and reasonable care when serving customers.

I’m quite disappointed with my experience at Supercheap Auto Dandenong.

A couple of days ago, I placed a Click & Collect order for a RUPES D-A Ultra-Fine Polishing Foam Pad 130/150mm at the Narre Warren store. I was later contacted and told the product was not actually available, and my money was refunded.

Today, I checked the Supercheap Auto website and saw the same product showing as available at the Dandenong store. As I was heading to work, I went out of my way to visit the store to purchase it.

When I arrived, I asked a staff member about the product and was directed to aisle 15. I couldn't find it, so I asked again. Another staff member checked aisle 15 and initially brought me a 125mm pad, which was not the product I was looking for. He then checked the drawers, but the product couldn't be located. He also contacted someone to check the warehouse, but they couldn't find any stock there either.

As I was leaving disappointed, I was told by another staff member that “it might be stolen.” I found this explanation surprising. If the website says the product is available, customers reasonably expect that the store actually has the product in stock. If the item is missing, misplaced or the stock count is incorrect, the online inventory should ideally be updated.

The staff were generally polite and did try to look for the item, so my main frustration isn't with the employees themselves. My concern is the inaccurate stock information, which resulted in me making an unnecessary trip to the store.

I hope Supercheap Auto can improve the accuracy of its store inventory system so customers can rely on the availability shown online, particularly when travelling to a store specifically to collect or purchase an item.

one_star_reviews.text: Yesterday, I visited the Puma store at DFO Moorabbin with my wife and two young children. While I was looking at shoes a short distance away, an older male staff member asked if my three-year-old daughter was mine. I said yes, apologised immediately, and called her over. He told me she had touched one of the bottles displayed in an open box on the floor near the checkout and said, “It’s not allowed to touch. We have to sterilise it. Look after your kid.” I completely understand hygiene concerns, but the way this was communicated felt abrupt and disrespectful, especially as I had apologised right away. After taking a moment to understand what had happened, I noticed there were no signs saying customers shouldn’t touch the bottles, and because the box was on the floor within easy reach of toddlers, I was genuinely unsure what the expectation was. When I later asked the cashier if customers were allowed to handle the bottles before buying, she said yes. After I explained why I was asking, another female staff member said my daughter had actually licked the bottle, not just touched it, which was different from what I had been told initially and left me confused. My concern isn’t about maintaining hygiene standards. I understand and respect that. It is about the way I was spoken to, and the inconsistent explanation. A more respectful and professional approach would have made the situation much easier to understand and resolve. I hope this feedback helps improve both customer communication and consideration of product placement when items are within easy reach of young children

Why doesn't the service have enough rooms available and staff to service the amount of clients coming and going? And can the receptionist stop being so naive about the women's hormones when visiting the clinic. one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience.
We came to Monash Health – Berwick Community Health Centre simply seeking practical support to help our daughter return to school after a difficult school experience.
Instead, we were drawn into around seven months of appointments, assessments and procedures with no meaningful solution or progress.
The service we experienced was very poor and lacked professionalism. We felt there was far too much focus on appointments, assessments and procedures, rather than finding a practical solution for our daughter.
Most concerningly, we felt that the constant focus on psychological assessments and labels increased our daughter’s distress rather than helping her. She became increasingly unhappy, while the original goal—helping her return to school—remained unresolved.
I am sharing this review to warn other parents: if your child needs urgent and practical support, make sure you understand from the beginning what concrete help will actually be provided and how long it will take.
Children need timely, professional and practical support—not months of appointments without meaningful outcomes.

I would not recommend Carpet Call Fyshwick based on my experience.
My insurer arranged for Carpet Call to complete flooring and skirting board installation works at my home in November 25 following significant sewage overflow damage, and I personally paid for flooring in two additional rooms at a cost of over $6,500.

Unfortunately, the overall experience became extremely stressful and disappointing.
On the day of installation, I was unexpectedly required to pay an additional $270 for furniture moving or the installers would not proceed with the work. I stayed for a short time initially as I had to work however I saw an installer using the affected toilet which I had warned them not to use as it could initiate another overflow. As we were not living at the house, I came back the next day to find cigarette butts all over my front lawn and pushed into my back deck along with discarded rubbish.

During the installation process, my dining table (purchased for $2,200 in 2024 and previously in excellent condition) was damaged after being moved by the installers. The damage included a split/detached leg as well as cracking to the tabletop.
In addition, I repeatedly raised concerns regarding the quality of the skirting board installation, including visible gaps, rough joins and poor finishing.
Over approximately 7 months I made numerous phone calls, texts and in-person visits attempting to resolve both the table damage and the workmanship concerns.

Initially, Carpet Call Fyshwick discussed repairs, compensation and skirting rectification works, including a scheduled repair date. However, after I continued raising concerns about the extent of the damage and workmanship issues, the agreed rectification works were later withdrawn, zero compensation was paid and the responsibility for the damage was disputed.

I found the overall handling of the matter disappointing due to the delays, lack of accountability and stress involved in trying to achieve a fair resolution. The company have now referred me to go through the ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal and said they would answer any further questions which I did have, I texted them back with no response.

So after paying a total of $6,797.13, I have been left with a significantly damaged dining table, skirting boards with visible gaps, amateur joins and poor finishing, and no meaningful resolution or any compensation despite months of attempting to resolve the matter directly with Carpet Call Fyshwick.

————————————————

John,

I do have several concerns regarding the statements made.
Firstly, I would be interested to understand how your "furniture experts" concluded that the installers did not damage my dining table. Neither expert attended my home at the time of the installation works, and the table was in excellent condition prior to the installers moving it. No one other than the flooring installers moved the table.
Secondly, your response refers to an $805 table leg repair. However, the text message I received from you stated that the repair quote was approximately $220 plus GST. These figures do not appear consistent. I also never received any refund of the $270 furniture moving fee.
I also dispute your statement regarding painting of the skirting boards. At no stage was I offered painting as a resolution. My concerns have always related to the visible gaps, poor joins and overall finish of the skirting boards. Painting would not rectify those issues.
Further, no other tradespeople were working in my home on the day the flooring installers attended. I personally observed the installers smoking repeatedly outside the property.
Finally, I find it difficult to reconcile your statement that you remain open to further discussion when it was your company that advised unresolved matters should be determined through ACAT and withdrew the previously scheduled rectification works.

Absolutely appalling — Coles customer service at its worst

I am absolutely appalled, disgusted and outraged by my experience at Coles today.

The supermarket was packed with customers, yet despite a large, clear and unmistakable sign at the entrance stating that NO DOGS are permitted inside the store, a customer was casually walking his dog through the aisles as though the rules simply did not apply to him.

This was clearly not a working assistance dog, and yet not a single staff member appeared to have the initiative, professionalism or basic common sense to intervene. The level of complacency was extraordinary. Staff were standing by while a blatant breach of the store’s own policy was taking place right in front of them.

But what happened when I raised the issue was even more infuriating.

Rather than acknowledging a perfectly legitimate concern, the checkout assistant was rude, arrogant, dismissive and downright smart-aleck. Her attitude was completely unacceptable and demonstrated an astonishing lack of respect for a paying customer. There was no attempt to listen, no professionalism and certainly no sense that customer concerns actually mattered.

Quite frankly, if this is the standard of customer service Coles is prepared to tolerate, it is nothing short of disgraceful.

Rules mean absolutely nothing if staff are unwilling to enforce them. And customer service means absolutely nothing if customers who raise legitimate concerns are treated with arrogance and contempt.

I have never been so disappointed by the complete lack of accountability and professionalism in a supermarket. What should have been a simple matter of enforcing a clearly displayed rule turned into an experience that left me feeling completely disrespected as a customer.

Coles needs to seriously question what is happening in this store. Complacency is not customer service. Indifference is not customer service. And treating customers with arrogance when they raise a legitimate concern is certainly not customer service.

I will be taking my business elsewhere. After today’s experience, I have absolutely no intention of returning to this Coles.

An extremely disappointing experience from start to finish — and one that Coles should be thoroughly embarrassed by.

We had seen the advertisements for the breakfast buffet at this restaurant and were really looking forward to coming. We had good experience with  Rashey restaurant before and were excited to try this branch, but unfortunately, we were extremely disappointed with our experience.

First of all, it was advertised as a buffet breakfast, but it honestly did not feel like a buffet at all. The eggs, sausages and ham were very poor in taste and quality. There was also a very limited amount of pancakes.

The restaurant opens at 9:00 am, and we arrived at around 9:10 am, yet almost all of the food trays were already empty. We waited for refills several times, but even when food was refilled, the quantities were extremely small — it seemed like each refill was enough for only 7–8 people. For example, when pancakes were brought out, if the people already waiting at the buffet took them, there was basically nothing left for anyone else.

The variety was also very disappointing. Milk, cereal and tea bags are standard items that you would expect at almost any breakfast buffet, so there was really nothing special about the selection. The overall quality was very average, the portions available at the buffet were far too small, and the variety was extremely limited.

Another disappointing point was the coffee. It was not included in the buffet price, so you had to pay extra for it. On top of that, it took an extremely long time to arrive — we waited around 30 minutes for our coffee.

Overall, we were not satisfied with the experience at all. The advertising felt quite misleading, especially considering what we expected from a breakfast buffet.

I usually leave positive reviews for places I visit when I have a good experience, so I don’t normally write negative reviews. However, this time I felt it was important to share our experience so that other customers know what to expect.

Unfortunately, we won’t be coming back and I would not recommend the breakfast buffet.
